The first release since fufu went public, and mostly about what you look at.

v0.1.0 could capture everything and hand it back; it just showed you the result in git's vocabulary. This release rewrites the views around the change instead of around the file list, and adds the commands you need to run fufu day to day without reaching past it.

**The views**

- `ff log` is change-centric. The `@` row is your open change and the `●` rows are commits, each carrying the tip of its segment — so the timeline reads as lines of work rather than as a flat list of snapshots. `ff evolog` is the other half: the open change's own snapshot chain, every capture that got you here.
- `ff status` shows one list of files, not three. fufu has no concept of tracked versus untracked or staged versus unstaged — the working tree *is* the change, whole — so there is nothing to sort files into. You get a diffstat: kind, path, lines added and removed, and a bar scaled to the widest change, under a two-row crop of `ff log` showing the open change and the commit beneath it.
- Snapshot ids are spelled in jj's reverse-hex alphabet, so an id reads as letters (`kzrn`) and can never be mistaken for a commit sha. Unique prefixes are highlighted as you go, and `ff restore --at` takes either spelling.
- Output is paged when it's a terminal and plain when it isn't, and the tool has a palette. `fufu.theme` picks it: `muted` by default, `vivid` for the saturated cut, `terminal` to drop to the base sixteen and inherit whatever you have already tuned. Color marks roles rather than commands, so one meaning gets one color everywhere it turns up — `ff doctor`'s WARN and a rebase that would conflict are the same orange because they mean the same thing.

**Running it**

- `ff config` reads and writes fufu's settings as plain `fufu.*` git config, through a typed registry that knows what exists, what it defaults to, and whether a value will parse. Eight settings so far: `maxFileSize`, `keep`, `autoTrim`, `pager`, `updateCheck`, `autoUpdate`, `trunk`, `theme`.
- `ff doctor` verifies the safety net end to end — chains, identity, reflogs, the gc guard, and whether your hooks are actually wired — and exits nonzero when it finds something.
- `ff update` replaces this binary with the latest release. `ff --version` now names the build it came from, sha and date, so a bug report says which one.
- `ff help <verb>` is a written page per verb, not a flag dump.
- Retention enforces itself: set `fufu.autoTrim` and old snapshots age out on a cadence instead of waiting for you to remember `ff trim`.

**`ff start`**

`ff new` is now `ff start` — it fetches trunk, forks from the fetched tip, and hands you a clean tree, so new work begins from what's actually on the remote rather than from wherever you happened to be standing. Nothing to name up front; fufu mints a name and you claim it once the work has earned one. `ff new` still works as an alias.

**Speed**

Snapshot ids resolve through an index, so a prefix costs the rows on your screen instead of a walk down the whole chain, and `ff log` hops segment to segment rather than stepping through every snapshot between commits. There is a benchmark suite behind this that gates on growth slopes rather than on milliseconds, so the property under test is that these stay flat as history gets deeper — which is the claim that matters on a repository you have had for years.

**Breaking: `--json` shapes**

Anything parsing fufu's JSON should look before upgrading.

- `ff status --json` drops `staged`, `unstaged`, and `untracked`. In their place: `changes` (per-file entries with path, kind, insertions, deletions), `insertions`, `deletions`, `open`, and `parent`. `head`, `operation`, `upstream`, and `conflicts` are unchanged.
- `ff log --json` retired `timeline` and gained `open`, describing the open change directly.

**Also**

Windows usage lines say `ff` rather than `ff.exe`. Dependency licenses are gated in CI to permissive-only. `make` is a fast dogfood build for daily use, with `make release` staying the honest fat-LTO one.

Install: see the [README](https://github.com/tyler-johnson/fufu#install) — `curl | sh`, PowerShell, or `brew install tyler-johnson/tap/fufu`. Already on v0.1.0? `ff update`.

Binaries for linux/darwin/windows × amd64/arm64, checksummed. The design — what exists, what's coming, and why — lives in [DESIGN.md](https://github.com/tyler-johnson/fufu/blob/main/DESIGN.md).
